prompt:
Write 11 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a low-speed head-on collision claim, in time order. Injury: whiplash. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1087; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment ran somewhat longer than usual for this injury.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- It is not fully clear where in the vehicle the claimant was sitting.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim reported by the insured's policyholder after a low-speed head-on collision in a parking area. The claimant reports neck pain and has retained counsel, who has asked that all contact go through their office.

Entry 2: Confirmed the driver is named on the policy and the coverage was in force at the time of loss. No issues with the policy terms have been found.

Entry 3: Reviewed photos from the scene and the other driver's statement. Both describe the same sequence of events and the point of contact between the two vehicles.

Entry 4: Witness statements were obtained and match the account given by both drivers. Nothing in the file contradicts how the collision occurred.

Entry 5: Vehicle inspection completed. The damage pattern is consistent with the impact described and the estimated repair is in line with a collision of this speed.

Entry 6: Checked prior claims and vehicle history. No earlier damage to this vehicle has been found in any records reviewed, and nothing suggests the damage predates the policy start.

Entry 7: Claimant's account was taken again through counsel. The description of the collision and the symptoms that followed matches what was given in the first report.

Entry 8: Medical records received. The reported injury, a soft tissue strain to the neck, is a typical result of a collision with this force. No prior treatment to the neck or upper back appears in the records.

Entry 9: Treatment has continued for somewhat longer than is usual for this type of injury. The treating provider's notes give reasons for the extended course, and we are requesting further detail.

Entry 10: Clarification requested from counsel on where the claimant was seated at impact, as the statements so far do not fully settle this. The answer may affect how the injury is assessed.

Entry 11: Claim remains open pending the seating position response and the final treatment report. No reason to dispute the core facts of the loss at this stage.
